# openprovider_glue_record (Resource)

Publishes the addresses of a nameserver named under a domain you hold, so that the domain can be delegated to a nameserver inside itself.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A nameserver named inside the domain it serves needs glue: the registry must
# publish its addresses, because nothing else can resolve the name.
resource "openprovider_glue_record" "ns1" {
  domain    = "example.com"
  subdomain = "ns1"

  ips = ["192.0.2.1", "2001:db8::1"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The domain the nameserver is named under (e.g., example.com).
- `ips` (Set of String) The addresses to publish for the nameserver. IPv4 and IPv6 are told apart by their form, and Openprovider holds at most one of each.
- `subdomain` (String) The label of the nameserver under the domain, without the domain itself (e.g., ns1).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The full host name of the nameserver, which is also the key Openprovider stores it under.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a glue record by the full host name of the nameserver.
terraform import openprovider_glue_record.ns1 ns1.example.com
```
